supporting_evidence.quote: The growth in R&D expense during 2025 compared to 2024 was primarily driven by increases in headcount-related expenses and infrastructure-related costs.

The growth in research and development expense during the second quarter and first six months of 2025 compared to the same periods in 2024 was driven primarily by increases in headcount-related expenses and infrastructure-related costs.

input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I found no evidence that contradicts or weakens the claim.

H1 (Infrastructure costs contributing more than headcount): The newly retrieved evidence (E7-E9) discusses gross margin drivers for Products and Services, not R&D expense drivers. None of the evidence provides quantitative breakdowns showing infrastructure costs exceeded headcount costs as a driver of R&D growth. NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE.

H2 (Other significant drivers like stock-based compensation, materials, facilities): The newly retrieved evidence (E10-E12) discusses general R&D activities, supply chain concentrations, and trade restrictions, but does not identify any specific R&D expense drivers beyond what was already stated in the original evidence. There is no mention of stock-based compensation, materials, or facilities as drivers of R&D expense growth in fiscal 2025. NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE.

H3 (Quantitative breakdowns showing infrastructure or other factors contributed more): The newly retrieved evidence (E13-E15) discusses tax provisions, interest rate risk, and intellectual property, but provides no quantitative breakdown of R&D expense components or drivers. NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE.

The original evidence remains unchallenged. All three quarterly filings (E1, E3) and the annual 10-K (E2) consistently state that R&D expense growth in fiscal 2025 was "primarily driven by increases in headcount-related expenses and infrastructure-related costs," with headcount listed first. The claim that growth was "driven mainly by higher headcount-related costs" is supported by this consistent attribution across all filings.
